haiku-low.q1: It signs in normally. Users are found by Google's permanent sub, not email, so the Gmail change is irrelevant. Google sign-in never changes users.email.
haiku-low.q2: The user must enter the existing account's password on the confirm page. Only a correct password inserts the user_identities row and calls start_session.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins. The 5th locks the account for 15 minutes, resets failed_logins to 0, and deletes the pending link. Nothing gets linked.
haiku-low.q4: A verified email matching no user creates a user with no password and a verified email, inserts the link, and calls start_session. Unverified email: refused, user told to use email and password, nothing created.
haiku-low.q5: Both cases give an error page and change nothing. After 10 minutes the state has expired. A reloaded callback finds the state already deleted, since it works once.
haiku-low.q6: start_session creates a new sessions row and sets a new sid cookie. What happens to an existing sid cookie is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required, only a signed-in session. If that Google account is linked to anyone, Settings refuses and nothing changes.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis key oidc:state:<state>, which holds state, nonce, verifier, purpose, user id and next page. The callback deletes it in one step, or it expires after 10 minutes.
haiku-low.q9: The pending link (sub, user id, next page) is in Redis oidc:confirm:<token>. The browser holds the token in HttpOnly cookie oidc_confirm. Success, lockout, or 10-minute expiry deletes it.
haiku-low.q10: In the user_identities table with user_id and google_sub. Both columns are unique, which enforces one Google account per user and one user per Google account.
haiku-low.q11: The user sees an error message on the start page. Whether the exchange is retried is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q12: The purpose (login or link) and user id are saved in the Redis attempt. For link, the sid session user must match the saved user id, otherwise it is refused.

sonnet.q1: Nothing changes for them. Linked users are found by `sub`, never by email, so the `sub` is found in `user_identities` and `start_session` is called. The document does not mention the Gmail address change.
sonnet.q2: The user must confirm the existing account's password. The callback saves a pending link (`oidc:confirm:<token>`), sets the `oidc_confirm` cookie and shows the confirm password page. The user must submit the correct password while the account is not locked and within 10 minutes. Then the `user_identities` row is inserted, the pending link is deleted and `start_session` is called. Preconditions: email_verified is true and that user has no other Google account.
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to `failed_logins`, and the user stays on the confirm page. On the 5th failure `locked_until` is set to now plus 15 minutes, `failed_logins` is reset to 0, and the pending link is deleted. The user sees the locked message and no link is created. If the account is already locked, the pending link is deleted and the cookie cleared without checking the password.
sonnet.q4: Verified email matching no user: a new user is created with no password and a verified email, the `user_identities` link is inserted, and `start_session` is called with no password confirmation. If the insert fails on the unique email, an error page is shown and nothing changes. Email not verified: the sign-in is refused, nothing is created, and the login page tells the user to use email and password.
sonnet.q5: Both cases give an error page and nothing changes. A callback after 12 minutes finds the state entry expired, since it lasts 10 minutes. A second load finds it already used, since the callback deletes the entry in one step.
sonnet.q6: `start_session` creates a `sessions` row, sets the `sid` cookie and redirects. This is the same call that password login makes. NOT STATED for what happens to a `sid` cookie the browser already had.
sonnet.q7: No password and no email match are required, and a verified Google email is not required either (noted as an open question to confirm). The user must be signed in, and the `sid` cookie must belong to the user id saved in the attempt. If the Google `sub` is already linked to anyone, or the user already has a Google account, the link is refused. Settings shows a refusal message and nothing changes.
sonnet.q8: They are kept in Redis under `oidc:state:<state>`, along with the purpose, the user id (link only) and the next page. The browser also holds the `oidc_state` cookie with the state value. Only the hash of the verifier goes to Google. The callback reads and deletes the entry in one step and clears the cookie. The entry otherwise expires after 10 minutes, as does the cookie.
sonnet.q9: It is held in Redis as `oidc:confirm:<token>` with the `sub`, user id and next page. The browser refers to it through the HttpOnly cookie `oidc_confirm`, which holds the token. It lasts up to 10 minutes. It is deleted on success, on lockout (the fifth wrong password, or an already locked account), or when it expires.
sonnet.q10: It is stored in the `user_identities` table, with columns `user_id` and `google_sub`. Each column is unique, which gives one Google account per user and one user per Google account. Rows last until Unlink or until the user is deleted.
sonnet.q11: The user is returned to the start page (login page for login, Settings for link) with an error message, and nothing new changes. NOT STATED whether the exchange is retried. The document gives no retry, and the timeout value is not yet set.
sonnet.q12: Start saves the purpose (`login` or `link`) in the Redis state entry, and the callback reads it back. For a link, the signed-in user id is saved in the attempt. The callback checks that the `sid` cookie belongs to that saved user id. If the session user has changed, the link is refused.
